profile.reading:
Per NTT's own Global Data Centers facility page, this building, NTT Chicago CH1, is located at 255 Pierce Rd, Itasca, IL 60143. The operator publishes 126,000 square feet of data floor space and 36 megawatts of critical IT load for this specific building; no formal certifications or opening year are stated on the page. CH1 anchors a roughly 19-acre, 200-plus-megawatt Chicago-area data center campus in Itasca, DuPage County, that NTT has continued to expand with additional buildings.

Illinois's data center tax incentive program has become a flashpoint for state energy policy. Governor JB Pritzker announced on June 5, 2026 a temporary suspension of new awards under the state's Data Center Investment Program, citing grid strain; ComEd's CEO stated the program had added roughly $12 a month to the average residential bill over the prior four years, and the move followed the state legislature's failure to pass the POWER Act (HB 5513) by its May 31, 2026 deadline. From 2020 through 2024, 27 data centers statewide received more than $983 million in tax incentives under the program, which was enacted in 2019 and offers up to 20 years of sales-tax exemption for qualifying $250 million-plus investments. ComEd's northern Illinois service territory is separately projected to face capacity shortfalls beginning around 2029 as data center demand grows, a dynamic pushing new development toward Chicago's southern suburbs where power is more readily available, according to legal-industry analysis of ComEd's planning filings.

NTT's US Global Data Centers footprint spans seven named campuses in total: Ashburn, Virginia at 224 megawatts; Chicago, Illinois at more than 200 megawatts; Dallas, Texas at 160 megawatts; Hillsboro, Oregon at 126 megawatts; Phoenix, Arizona at 240 megawatts; and a combined Sacramento/Santa Clara, California figure of 68 megawatts, totaling roughly 1,118 megawatts or more of disclosed US capacity, per the operator's own locations page. The US business operates under the NTT DATA Global Data Centers Americas name, the successor brand to RagingWire Data Centers, now under Japan's NTT DATA Group and parent Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corporation, a Tokyo Stock Exchange-listed company not subject to SEC 10-K filing requirements.

reading.body:
NTT Chicago CH1 has 36 MW of published IT capacity, making it one of six Illinois data centers that disclose load figures and accounting for 15 percent of the state's total disclosed capacity.

Illinois maps 44 data center facilities but only six publish their power consumption. This transparency gap means 38 mapped sites remain invisible to grid planning. For a state trying to anticipate AI infrastructure demands, the absence of these numbers creates a blind spot. NTT's willingness to publish its capacity is unusual enough to be notable.

Whether NTT Chicago CH1 can actually handle large-scale AI training is unknowable from its published specifications. The facility discloses power draw but not electrical service rating, cooling capability, or grid qualifications. These constraints matter more than headline capacity for AI workloads, which pack 40 kW or more into single racks. A 36 MW facility could hold 900 racks at typical AI density, but only if the building's infrastructure supports it.

The data shows what one operator chose to tell the market, not what grid planners need to know. Illinois's capacity visibility problem is common. Without disclosure from all operators, forecasting power demand for AI infrastructure remains guesswork.
